hook.line: Sometimes the best way to say "that's not like you" or "that's typical of this place" is a single small adjective. It lets you comment on behaviour without accusing anyone.
hook.es: Esa actitud no es propia de un profesional.
hook.en: That attitude isn't what you'd expect from a professional.

examples.es: Esa actitud no es propia de un profesional.
examples.en: That attitude isn't what you'd expect from a professional.

examples.es: Es un plato propio de la costa.
examples.en: It's a dish typical of the coast.

examples.es: No es propio de Vale llegar tarde.
examples.en: It isn't like Vale to arrive late.

examples.es: Estas lluvias son propias de abril.
examples.en: These rains are typical of April.

examples.es: Los tintos fuertes son propios de este barrio.
examples.en: Strong black coffees are typical of this neighbourhood.
Is it like you to complain so much? (to a friend)

rule:
*Ser propio de* means "to be typical of" or "to be what you'd expect from".

It works two ways: describing what belongs to a place or time (*un plato propio de la costa*), or what fits a person (*es propio de Vale*).

With *no*, it becomes a gentle criticism: this behaviour doesn't fit.

*Propio* is an adjective, so it agrees with the thing described: *propio, propia, propios, propias*. It is followed by *de*, never *a* or *para*. (Don't mix it up with *mi propio carro*, "my own car".)
smallPrint: Teachers call this *adjective plus preposition*: *propio* needs *de* to complete its meaning.

readAndPick.es: Esa actitud no es propia de un profesional.
options: That attitude is typical of a professional.
That attitude isn't what you'd expect from a professional.
That professional has no attitude.

readAndPick.es: Es un plato propio de la costa.
options: It's a dish typical of the coast.
It's a dish from far away.
It's a dish nobody eats on the coast.

readAndPick.es: No es propio de Vale llegar tarde.
options: Vale likes arriving late.
It isn't like Vale to arrive late.
Vale arrived late.

readAndPick.es: Estas lluvias son propias de abril.
options: This rain is typical of April.
These rains are typical of April.
These rains came in April.

readAndPick.es: Los tintos fuertes son propios de este barrio.
options: Strong black coffees are typical of this neighbourhood.
The strong black coffee is typical of this neighbourhood.
Strong black coffees are not typical of this neighbourhood.
Is it like you to complain so much? (to a friend)
Is it like him to complain so much?
Do you complain about yourself so much? (to a friend)

readAndPick.es: Esa risa es propia de Hernando.
options: That laugh is typical of Hernando.
Hernando has his own laugh.
Hernando never laughs like that.

readAndPick.es: Mentir no es propio de ella.
options: She lies a lot.
Lying isn't like her.
She didn't lie.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *propio* or *propia* and type the whole sentence: *Esa actitud no es ___ de un profesional.*
yourTurn.answer: Esa actitud no es propia de un profesional.
yourTurn.why: *Actitud* is feminine, so the adjective is *propia*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: It's a dish typical of the coast.
yourTurn.answer: Es un plato propio de la costa.
accept: Es un plato típico de la costa.
yourTurn.why: *Plato* is masculine singular, so it takes *propio*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: These rains are typical of April.
yourTurn.answer: Estas lluvias son propias de abril.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: It isn't like Vale to arrive late.
yourTurn.answer: No es propio de Vale llegar tarde.
accept: Llegar tarde no es propio de Vale.
yourTurn.why: *No es propio de* plus a name says it doesn't fit that person.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative: *Mentir es propio de ella.* Say: Lying isn't like her.
yourTurn.answer: Mentir no es propio de ella.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it plural: *El tinto fuerte es propio de este barrio.* Say: Strong black coffees are typical of this neighbourhood.
yourTurn.answer: Los tintos fuertes son propios de este barrio.
yourTurn.why: Everything agrees in the plural: *los tintos fuertes son propios*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, asking a friend: Is it like you to complain so much?
yourTurn.why: *De ti* names the person, so you ask whether it fits them.

pitfalls.wrong: Esa actitud no es propio de un profesional.
pitfalls.right: Esa actitud no es propia de un profesional.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Propio* agrees with what it describes, and *actitud* is feminine.

pitfalls.wrong: Estas lluvias son propias a abril.
pitfalls.right: Estas lluvias son propias de abril.

pitfalls.wrong: Es un plato propia de la costa.
pitfalls.right: Es un plato propio de la costa.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Plato* is masculine, so you need *propio*.

personal: Say one thing that is typical of your city, or of someone you know, using *propio de*.
